To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recurrent neural networks are capable of knowledge transfer between related tasks and can be used for model-based control of complex systems.

(i) recurrent neural networks can be used for data-driven system identification of dynamical systems, and (ii) recurrent neural networks allow for efficient transfer of knowledge from one or multiple related tasks to a task that lacks sufficient amount of data.

1) the proposed model architecture for knowledge transfer is capable of learning the underlying dynamics of the target system and of transferring information from one or multiple sources to the target system, and 2) the model can be trained efficiently and can be adapted for fully observable and partially observable system identiﬁcation tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of data-driven recurrent neural network models for knowledge transfer and their application to system identification.
recurrent neural networks for data-driven system identification.
the design of recurrent neural network architectures for data-efficient system identification of technical systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented recurrent neural network architectures are a promising approach to transfer knowledge among tasks and improve data-efficiency in the context of dynamical system modeling.

the proposed recurrent neural network architectures are capable of learning the dynamics of complex systems from limited data and that knowledge transfer can be achieved by means of dual-task learning, mult-task learning, or transfer learning.

the recurrent network architecture developed in this thesis is capable of knowledge transfer in a variety of scenarios, and that the knowledge transfer can be improved by using auxiliary tasks with a higher level of observability than the target task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that knowledge transfer can be successfully employed in the context of data-driven system identification.

we have developed a novel recurrent neural net- work architecture that can be applied to different knowledge transfer scenarios, i.e. dual-task, multi-task, and transfer learning, in order to improve the learning of the target task.
we have developed a new recurrent neural network architecture that is capable of knowledge transfer between multiple related tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

recurrent neural networks are a powerful tool for knowledge transfer and that the proposed model is able to improve data-efficiently the model of a target system by means of data from one or several source systems.
knowledge transfer can significantly improve the accuracy of data-driven system identification models.
recurrent neural networks can be used to transfer knowledge from one or multiple auxiliary tasks to a target task in a data-efficient manner.
